chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) would greet the women, and they would return the greeting to him; and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would greet the women, and he disliked greeting the young woman among them, saying: 'I fear that her voice might please me, so what enters upon me [in terms of distraction/feeling] would be more than what I seek from the reward.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali (AS) dislike greeting young women?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the nuanced Shia jurisprudence regarding gender interaction, distinguishing between the general permissibility of greeting women and the specific caution advised against young women. Imam Ali’s (AS) reasoning highlights the concept of *khawf al-shughl* (fear of distraction), where excessive sensory pleasure might diminish the sincerity (*ikhlas*) and thus the spiritual reward of the act. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on guarding the heart from minor distractions to maintain pure devotion in daily rituals.
